newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Reader's Digest urges media be global, speak local.
newsitem.headline: Reader's Digest urges media be global, speak local.

text.p: Fears that powerful global media groups will undermine cultural diversity are unfounded, James Schadt, the chairman and CEO of Reader's Digest Association Inc, said on Thursday.
Schadt, addressing an advertising conference, said there was no point in big media firms trying to market bland, homogenous material all around the world because it simply would not sell.
"It won't work because of a fundamental truth of the marketplace. That is, to be a growing, successful global player, you have to increase the diversity of your local content."
"To be blunt it means you can't force an undifferentiated product down different people's throats," he said.
The initial problems of the Euro Disney theme park near Paris, he said, had forced Walt Disney Co to rethink the project and pay more heed to European tastes.
Schadt said that, to be successful in local markets, it was essential to create and sell in the local language.
U.S.-based Reader's Digest, he said, published 48 editions in 19 languages with a third of the content written locally.
In Thailand, the magazine had achieved limited sales in Asian English and Chinese editions but when a Thai edition was launched its circulation rose to over 100,000 within a year.
"The pundits and editorial writers fear that cultural diversity will be wiped out in a world of global media giants. We think the opposite," he said.
"The major players not only have the scale and the resources to preserve diversity...it's in their best economic interests to do so," he said.
